input.rationale: Section 13.5 starts in the right place — Developments (software interface coding/programs created solely by Corio) are owned by us and Commerce One assigns any claim of ownership (p0116) — and Commerce One's retention of the Software under 2.8 is acceptable. However, the carve-out in p0115 flips ownership of IP created solely by our personnel to Commerce One whenever Commerce One supports it on an ongoing basis, with no licence back to us for those Developments. That is an assignment of Customer-created IP to the Vendor, which is walk-away territory under this rule and fails the fallback (no perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence back). The minimal fix deletes the carve-out so Developments are owned by Corio, subject to Commerce One's pre-existing ownership; if support is the driver we can offer Commerce One a support-purposes licence instead. Noted but not separately flagged: the agreement has no express Customer Data ownership sentence (data is covered only by the confidentiality/NDA regime at Section 10), and ownership of enhancements to the Software itself is left to future negotiation rather than allocated to us.

proposal.summary: Remove the carve-out that gives Commerce One ownership of Developments created solely by Corio where Commerce One supports them.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We own the Developments our personnel create, so we have deleted the carve-out transferring ownership to Commerce One wherever it provides ongoing support; Commerce One's pre-existing materials and the Software remain its property. If ongoing support is the concern, we can instead grant Commerce One a licence to use those Developments for support purposes.
